_about: Everything about how the video LOOKS and SAYS. No code changes needed for any of this.
fps_note: Default render profile: 1920x1080 at 30 fps (formats.landscape). Allowed test profile: 1280x720 at 24 fps, for small tests and if it plays smoother overall (Charles, 2026-11-21). See 'profiles'.

test._hint: Allowed for small tests or if it comes out smoother. Stage pixel values scale by H/1080.

fade_note: Crossfade retired as the default (Charles, 2026-11-21: 'Crossfade is probably worse'). A crossfade between full-body drawings shows two bodies mid-fade (D-14). Loops are built with pinned first and last frames instead: keyframed compositing or interpolation from approved poses, or generated video pinned on the approved pose at both ends so the last frame matches the first. The old value was 0.3; the kit still honours a positive value if someone wants to compare.

stage._about: The approved one-camera stage (Charles, 2026-11-21, mockup v3). One camera, no zoom, no camera move. Values are for the default 1920x1080 profile; for 1280x720 multiply by 2/3.
stage.camera: fixed: no zoom, no pan, no cut between exercises
stage.lying_scale_rule: Lying and floor figures are scaled UP relative to the standing scale, by lying_scale_multiplier, so the boy looks comparable in size lying and standing. This replaces the old rule that made floor figures smaller (video/chart.py DEPTH 0.88 and the kit 'fit' 0.72 to 0.78 in config/strips.json). The value is the midpoint of the two lying scales compared in layout mockup v2: large enough to read clearly, without the earlier 'giant guy'.
stage.calibration: Measure scale on head landmarks (ear height, and hairline to chin), not the bounding box. A bounding box changes with the pose; the head does not.
stage.head_crop: The head is never cropped in any frame of any pose (YouTube MznqHWzCv8s is the counter-example).
stage.fill: The boy fills the frame as much as the head-never-cropped rule allows.
stage.layers: Keep background, character and overlay as separate layers so versions are fast to make.
stage.status: Specification. The kit (kit/build.py) still sizes figures by box fit times 'fit'; porting this rule into the kit is open work.

recolor._hint: Hue in degrees (0 red, 52 yellow, 120 green, 210 blue, 280 purple). null leaves it alone.

backdrop._hint: Each layer (sky, clouds, mountains-far, mountains-near, trees-back, trees-front, ground) is its own file in assets/backdrops/<id>/<format>/. Swap one with overrides: {"clouds": "assets/backdrops/mine/clouds.png"}. style "image" uses one picture.

_chart_looks_hint: A chart can have its own room and props. Charts without an entry use "backdrop" above (the original code-drawn forest, retired for new rooms as they arrive). Add "scene": "config/scene.chartN.json" to give a chart its own props (a mat overlay).

overlay._about: Follow-along overlay in the style of Fraser Wilson's YouTube workouts (@FraserWilsonFit). Chosen by Charles 2026-11-21 over the old title, digital clock and bottom progress bar. Drawn on its own layer above the boy.

name_card.tip: ONE short form tip under the name, a few words

timer.shape: minimal ring timer (mockup C): a thin ring that empties as the exercise time runs down, seconds left in the middle

alternate._hint: Charles, 2026-11-21: 'We could try the bottom right and left'. Not approved; compare against the top layout before using.

overlay.status: Specification. The kit's Hud class still draws the legacy title, clock and bar from 'hud' and 'strings' above; those keys stay until the overlay is implemented.
